questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline handle automatically that a traditional notebook pipeline does not?
options: Retries, incremental state tracking, and orchestration order
Writing the actual PySpark transformation logic
Choosing which cloud provider to run on
Naming the output tables
questions.explain: Once tables are declared, Lakeflow automatically retries failed updates, tracks processed rows, and infers execution order.

questions.q: In a traditional notebook pipeline, what must you manage by hand that Lakeflow handles for you?
options: The checkpointLocation for incremental/streaming state
The name of the Python file
The Unity Catalog metastore region
The cluster's Databricks Runtime version
questions.explain: A traditional notebook pipeline requires manually managing a checkpointLocation, as Lesson 33 covered, instead of Lakeflow's automatic tracking.

questions.q: What real trade-off does this lesson identify regarding debugging?
options: A traditional notebook supports cell-by-cell debugging; a running Lakeflow pipeline is debugged as a whole graph instead
Lakeflow pipelines cannot be debugged at all
Traditional notebooks cannot be debugged interactively
Both approaches debug identically, with no real difference
questions.explain: This is a real adjustment, not a downgrade — debugging a pipeline means testing the function independently, then re-running the whole graph.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when is 'keep the notebook' the honest answer?
options: For a one-off exploratory script or a team still learning PySpark fundamentals
Whenever a pipeline has more than two tables
Never — Lakeflow is always the better choice
Only when the data is stored in Parquet format
questions.explain: A one-off script or ad-hoc pipeline that changes weekly often isn't worth Lakeflow's learning overhead yet.

questions.q: When does Lakeflow's automatic retry and dependency tracking start genuinely paying for itself, per this lesson?
options: A pipeline with real production SLAs, several interdependent tables, and years of expected maintenance
Only for pipelines with fewer than two tables
Only when running on an all-purpose cluster
Never — the overhead always outweighs the benefit
questions.explain: Real production SLAs and long-term maintenance are exactly where Lakeflow's automation earns its complexity.
